evidence.

marked entire police documents at Ex.P.1 to 7, 13 and
20.

So on perusal of these documents, it is clear that
the concerned I.O after investigation has filed
chargesheet against the offending water tanker driver
for the alleged offences punishable U/Sec 279, 338 of
Ipc and U/s 134( a & b) and Sec.187 of Imv Act for

tanker driver only.

water tanker driver after causing the accident did not

to a car.

It is true that in the Imv report got marked as
per Ex.P.6 it shows front damages to the motorcycle.

But by this only it cannot be assumed that the rider of
the motorcycle was negligent for the accident.

21 . It is admitted by all the petitioners that on
the date of accident three persons were proceeding in
the motorcycle against the traffic rules.

The concerned
I.O is silent in this regard in police records.

Hence on
this ground the respondents contend that there is
contributory negligence of the rider of motorcycle for
the accident.

At this stage the petitioners have relied
upon decision reported in
 a. 2016 Acj 383 - Chakali Swaroopa V/

evidence to establish negligence of the motorcyclist
because of triple riding then no contributory
negligence to be considered.

 d. 2014 Acj 2550 - Kiran V/s Sajjan singh -

It

22 . Therefore relying upon the above preposition
if we apply the same to the facts of this case then it is
clear that the respondents have not established the
negligence of the one of the petitioner/rider of
motorcycle for the accident.

It is true that eventhough
three persons were proceeding in a motorcycle by itself
will not amounts to negligence for the accident.

If at all
the rider of motorcycle by having two pillion riders
along with him lost control over the motorcycle and if it
leads to the accident then it amounts to contributory
negligence.
But in the instant case it is not so.

So
there is no supportive evidence on record to show that
by triple riding the accident occurred.
 (Scch3) 17 MVC.No.7387/19

 & Mvc.7389/19

So on perusal of all the police records
accompanied with the oral evidence of the Pw.1 to 3

in this regard, it is true that the petitioners have
proved that the offending water tanker driver was
involved in this accident and its driver due to his
negligent driving had caused the accident which leads
to injuries to petitioners.
 24.

Therefore with the available oral and
documentary evidence it is true that the petitioners
have proved that they have sustained injuries due to
the rash and negligent driving of the water tanker
driver.
